llm.summary: The skill is an instruction-only audit tool whose declared purpose, required footprint, and runtime instructions are consistent with a SKILL.md quality checker.

dimensions.detail: The name and description say this is a quality/audit tool for SKILL.md files and the package is instruction-only with no binaries, env vars, or install steps — everything requested (none) matches that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions tell the agent to locate and read target SKILL.md files (local paths across platforms) and include an example curl command to fetch raw files from GitHub. That is expected for an audit tool, but it does mean the agent will read files from your filesystem and can fetch remote SKILL.md content — both are necessary for the task but worth noting as data-access surface.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files — lowest-risk model (instruction-only). Nothing is downloaded or written to disk by an installer.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, credentials, or config paths. There are no disproportionate requests for secrets or unrelated service keys.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (default) and user-invocable:true. The skill does not request permanent presence or modify other skills; autonomous invocation is allowed by platform default but the skill itself doesn’t demand elevated persistence.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This appears to be a coherent, low-risk audit skill. Before running it, consider: (1) it will read SKILL.md files from locations you point it at (local skill directories listed in the instructions) — if you don’t want an agent to scan certain directories, don't point it there; (2) the examples show using curl to fetch raw SKILL.md from GitHub — only audit remote skills from trusted repositories, since fetching remote files can pull attacker-controlled content; (3) it requests no credentials and has no installer, so it won't exfiltrate secrets by design, but granting an autonomous agent permission to scan your filesystem increases exposure surface. If you prefer stricter control, run the audit manually (offline) or review the SKILL.md files yourself before invoking the skill.
